title: ClinicalTrials.gov: clinical-trial registry/results database as denominator visibility infrastructure
summary: ClinicalTrials.gov is encoded as denominator visibility infrastructure because it gives clinical studies public identifiers, registry records, protocol/result fields, responsible-party workflows, and summary-result surfaces even when publication is delayed, selective, or absent.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0008 as a denominator-visibility / registration-correction infrastructure record.

claims.claim: ClinicalTrials.gov is identified as a website and online database of clinical research studies and information about their results, making it a central registry/results surface for clinical research visibility.
what_would_change_status: ClinicalTrials.gov changes its stated purpose or database scope.

claims.claim: For NIH-funded clinical trials, NIMH/NIH policy context states that studies expected to register in ClinicalTrials.gov are also expected to report results; results are due no later than one year after primary completion and are submitted as summary modules including participant flow, baseline characteristics, outcome measures/statistical analyses, and adverse events.
what_would_change_status: NIH/NIMH or ClinicalTrials.gov revises registration/results policy or reporting modules.

claims.claim: The responsible party enters ClinicalTrials.gov registration data in the Protocol Registration and Results System; ClinicalTrials.gov staff review submissions, after which a successfully registered trial receives an NCT number and a public record.
what_would_change_status: ClinicalTrials.gov changes PRS workflow, staff review, NCT assignment, or public-posting sequence.

claims.claim: ClinicalTrials.gov is powerful denominator infrastructure but not a complete truth surface: scope, legal obligations, update quality, missing results, and discrepancies with publications require separate audit records.
what_would_change_status: Compliance audits and database sampling justify a narrower or stronger completeness claim.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no compliance audit, outcome evaluation, or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, process fields, and design tradeoffs; it does not estimate coverage, compliance, publication bias reduction, or outcome effects.
Registry presence is not evidence that a study was completed, well conducted, published, unpublished, null, or reported without discrepancies.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: United States/NIH/FDAAA context plus international discoverability; not all global trials and not all obligations are identical
reporter_protection_design: not a confidential reporting system; accountability is primarily public registration/results transparency rather than anonymity
limitations: individual participant data not collected in summary result modules
type_payload.query_value: Lets the cube ask whether a clinical study existed and whether summary results were reported even when journal publication is absent or selective.

handling_notes: Registries and post-publication platforms can make hidden or corrected research visible; they can also become instruments of reputational harm if treated as accusation surfaces.
Keep source, claim, study, result, correction, and comment separate. A platform record is not a verdict on any individual study or author.
Private, embargoed, or confidential records must not be bypassed; cite only public source metadata or ethically/lawfully available material.

unknowns: No database sampling was performed in rev0008.
Compliance, result-posting rates, selective public release, correction latency, and field-specific uptake remain open.
No individual trial, preregistration, Registered Report, retraction, or PubPeer thread record is promoted in this revision.
next_actions: Create a study-lifecycle record linking one public preregistration/registry record to its results, publication, and correction/update state.
Add compliance and coverage audits before treating any infrastructure as denominator-complete.
Add negative controls: registered studies whose records did not lead to public results, and public corrections that did not change practice.
